reason: E1 states HEAs have prominent mechanical characteristics and wear/corrosion resistance but does not mention cladding or tribo-corrosion. E2 studies a different HEA system (AlCoCrFeNiCuNb) and laser cladding, not microwave cladding of FeCoNiMnCu, so it does not directly support the specific composition or method. E3 shows nanocrystalline layers, twins, and dislocation activity in CoCrFeMnNi under dry sliding, but does not involve cladding, corrosion, or the FeCoNiMnCu system. The cited evidence thus provides only generic, indirect support for some premises and misrepresents the specific claims
premises: FeCoNiMnCu HEA exhibits solid solution strengthening and good wear/corrosion resistance
Cladding FeCoNiMnCu HEA onto a substrate improves tribological and corrosion properties
Tribo-corrosion of HEAs leads to nanocrystalline and oxide-rich subsurface layers
Solid solution strengthening reduces microstructural changes under tribological load
